subject: BRIGHTHARBOR: support & privilege evidence + retention clarifications
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BRIGHTHARBOR: support & privilege evidence + retention clarifications

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a few concrete asks so we can get procurement and security ops aligned before the demo: 

Summary of what we discussed
- BrightHarbor will need EU data residency for PII (production workspace and logs).
- Support access: SSO-backed jumpbox + time-limited break-glass flow with audit logging is preferred.
- Retention asks: 13 months for logs; 7 years for certain compliance records (procurement is asking).
- Field-level redaction / tokenization was mentioned as a potential requirement for a subset of PII.

Asks & next steps from Redwood
1) Can you confirm the AWS region that must host customer data? (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1)
2) Can you share a short list of PII categories (attached: example classification) and call out anything that must be redacted at ingestion?
3) Procurement requested a 1-pager evidence bundle (SOC2, tenancy isolation notes, logging retention policy) — can we confirm a recipient?
4) We'd like to schedule a 30–45m SecurOps walkthrough to go over the RBAC and break-glass mechanics. Is July 1 or July 2 morning CET possible?

I've attached an RBAC template and a draft mutual action plan to accelerate internal approvals. If it helps, Redwood can propose a Dedicated or Private deployment for strict data residency and support isolation.

I'll follow up with Vanessa to pull together the evidence bundle. Let me know answers to 1–3 and preferred meeting slot.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-rbac-proposal.csv (spreadsheet)

Cc: BrightHarbor Security <security@brightharbor.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: BRIGHTHARBOR: support & privilege evidence + retention clarifications

Thanks Sean — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Region: eu-west-1 is our preference for PII. We have EU contracts and our data residency policy requires that.
2) PII classification: I attached our internal classification PDF (quick list). For the purposes of this PoC, we need name, email, and national ID redacted at ingestion for the analytics pipeline. Log records (access logs, request traces) should be retained for 13 months; certain legal artifacts we retain for 7 years.
3) Support access: we can support SSO jumpbox + ephemeral admin elevation (break-glass) provided there's an automated approval audit and alerting to our SOC channel. We do not allow vendors to have persistent shell access to the production tenancy.
4) Procurement contact: Marta Lopez (marta.lopez@brightharbor.com) — she asked for a concise evidence bundle (1 page) including SOC2 Type II link, network isolation summary, and logging retention policy.

I'll attach the classification PDF now. We can meet July 1 at 10:00 CET for the walkthrough — that works for SOC and procurement.

Avery Collins
Senior Security Engineer, BrightHarbor
avery.collins@brightharbor.com

Notes for the walkthrough:
- We'll bring our SecurOps engineer and Vanessa will demo the RBAC matrix template (attached redwood-rbac-proposal.csv).
- For break-glass we propose: time-limited elevation tokens granted via an approval workflow, automatic session recording, and immutable audit logs forwarded to your SIEM/CloudWatch.
- Logging retention: Redwood default is 13 months for request logs; we can extend to 7 years for archival artifacts (offline storage) if required by contract.
- Evidence bundle: we'll provide SOC2 Type II report link (redacted for public), tenancy isolation note, and a short diagram of access paths.

Link to SOC2 (shared view): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/SOC2/REDWOOD-SOC2-TYPEII-2026
